body:
We discovered this issue due to https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/21059, which adds a test for `<input type=radio required name="">.validity.valueMissing`.

The spec doesn't really define what a [radio button group](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#radio-button-group) is. It only defines a relation between two distinct `input` elements, but does not answer the question of reflexivity.

I suppose there are two ways to make the definition firmer:

1. Imperatively, by defining when a radio button group is created and destroyed, and when an `<input>` element joins and leaves the radio button group.
2. Mathematically still, but in a consistent way that clearly answers the questions in the issue.

The first way sounds a bit like what @tkent-google is looking for, and is more or less what implementations actually do. But OTOH it sounds like it would be a lot of work, and the resultant spec could be bogged down by implementation details.

I propose defining radio button groups as equivalence classes over the set of all `<input>` elements, given [the relation currently in the spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#radio-button-group) except with reflexivity explicitly stated so that it is a proper equivalence relation. This would align with the current EdgeHTML/Gecko behavior, and make all `input` elements be associated with a radio button group at the spec level. As far as constraint validation is concerned, I don't really see too much reason in the current Chrome/Safari behavior: if a `<input type=radio>` without `name` is `required` but unchecked, it's reasonable to think that it's invalid.

Under this proposal, the answers to the questions would be the following:

> - Should `<input type=checkbox>` be in a radio button group?

Yes. The spec-level radio button group contains the `input` element itself and nothing else. But the answer doesn't really matter as it's not observable through any JavaScript or UI.

> - Should a radio button without `name` attribute be in a radio button group?

Yes. The radio button group contains the `input` element itself and nothing else. But this doesn't necessarily mean a new radio button group data structure has to be allocated in an implementation, since we know that unless the radio button gets a non-empty `name` attribute, it could never be group-mates with any other `input` elements. In this case, the `valueMissing` attribute can be then short-circuited to return the checkedness of the element.

The same should apply for radio buttons with an empty `name` attribute.

> - Should a radio button with a non-empty `name` attribute make a new radio button group if no suitable radio button group exist?

Yes. This should be the same as the status quo.

Here are some opinions and questions. Note that my opinions aren't very strongly held.

- Defining as an equivalence class does seem nicer than the current version of almost-an-equivalence-class.
- Allowing non-radio buttons to join the equivalence class seems strange, even if it's unobservable. Can we define it as an equivalence class over input type=radio, instead of over input? Or maybe it's simpler to say every input element has a radio button group...
- I'd rather match 2/3 (active) browsers, i.e. Chrome and Safari, than match 1/3, i.e. Firefox, for the no-name case. Is that possible without things getting really messy?
- We should consider adding a ton of examples to the spec after the definition of radio button group to illustrate all these subtleties.
- @tkent-google, as an implementer, how do you feel about an imperative description vs. a mathematical equivalence-class description?

> * Allowing non-radio buttons to join the equivalence class seems strange, even if it's unobservable. Can we define it as an equivalence class over input type=radio, instead of over input? Or maybe it's simpler to say every input element has a radio button group...

I also think allowing non-radio buttons is weird.



> * I'd rather match 2/3 (active) browsers, i.e. Chrome and Safari, than match 1/3, i.e. Firefox, for the no-name case. Is that possible without things getting really messy?

The cost of the change for empty-name radio buttons would be small.  It's acceptable to follow the EdgeHTML/Firefox behavior.

> * @tkent-google, as an implementer, how do you feel about an imperative description vs. a mathematical equivalence-class description?

I don't care about it.  Browsers already have stable implementations.  Imperative description won't help existing browsers a lot.
(It makes sense to me that `input` elements hold the group as we don't have hidden classes underneath `input` elements for the different types as some implementations do.)
